entities.name: The Iranian Zoroastrian Corpus
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Iranian Zoroastrian Corpus encompasses the sacred and theological literature of Zoroastrianism, one of the world's oldest monotheistic/dualistic religions, founded by the prophet Zarathushtra (Zoroaster, c. 1500–1000 BCE). Its core is the Avesta — liturgical texts in the Old Avestan and Younger Avestan languages, including the Gathas (hymns attributed to Zoroaster himself), the Yasna (liturgical texts), the Vendidad (laws of purity), and the Yashts (hymns to divinities).

Supplementing the Avesta is a rich body of Middle Persian (Pahlavi) theological, cosmological, and eschatological literature including the Bundahishn (cosmogony), Denkard (encyclopedia of Zoroastrian knowledge), and Arda Viraf Namag (a visionary journey to heaven and hell that prefigures Dante). Zoroastrian concepts of cosmic dualism, angels, demons, final judgment, heaven, hell, bodily resurrection, and a future savior profoundly influenced Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
